Article Title: Fleeing drowning scene not proof of culpability, says SC; acquits 2 held guilty of killing friend
Article Text:
An SC bench said the evidence for an accidental drowning was more plausible than homicide.

NEW DELHI: Observing that the human mind can sometimes act foolishly, especially in the face of unpredictable adversity, Supreme Court has said that such behaviour cannot be the sole basis of conviction and acquitted two men who had been held guilty of killing their friend.They were convicted by trial court and high court because their friend drowned in a river in their presence and instead of trying to rescue him, they left the spot and went to watch a movie, actions which were held as evidence of their culpability.Gujarat high court held that their behaviour was proof that they had killed the friend, and it was not a case of drowning in the river, sentencing them to life imprisonment.Setting aside the order of trial court and high court, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said there was no evidence to prove that it was a case of murder and held that the deceased had drowned accidentally."The accused are guilty of having fled from the spot and not having attempted to rescue the drowning person by crying out for help. Their conduct of having gone for a movie after witnessing their friend drowning, though reprehensible, cannot be found to be an incriminating circumstance, to establish murder rather than drowning. The hypothesis of innocence is crystal clear, and circumstances indicate an accident and not a premeditated murder," the bench said.Disagreeing with the findings of the HC, the bench said, "We also have to notice the high court's presumption that no person who saw his friend drowning would go to a movie or would take the trouble of bringing back empty soda bottles to the shop from where they purchased it. If such a presumption is accepted then it can be presumed that even after a premeditated murder, the accused would not conduct themselves in that manner. ""The human mind, as has often been held by this court, is at the same time fickle, manipulative and imaginative and the actions, the result of a deprived or a foolish mindset, especially in the face of adversities, cannot be predicted. The subsequent conduct on which the high court found possible the prosecution story of murder rather than of drowning, in this case we are unable to accept. It is the hypothesis of an accidental drowning that looms large from the evidence led at the trial; more plausible than a homicide," SC said.Challenging their conviction, the accused submitted that they, at worst, could be held guilty of a misadventure which turned fatal for their friend, and there was absolutely no evidence to prove even a homicidal death. They, however, admitted that they fled the scene in panic.
Article Summary: Supreme Court acquits two men who had been held guilty of killing their friend. They were convicted because their friend drowned in a river in their presence and instead of trying to rescue him, they left the spot and went to watch a movie. Supreme Court said the evidence for an accidental drowning was more plausible than homicide.

Article Title: From burnt cash to possibly the first impeachment of a judge: The Yashwant Varma saga explained
Article Text:
Yashwant Varma is likely to impeachment proceedings after a Parliamentary panel found all charges against him proved.

The night the cash was found

In-house probe

How did Parliament get involved?

Varma fights the inquiry

What did the Parliamentary inquiry find?

Why does Parliament still want to pursue impeachment?

Has any judge ever been impeached?

A test of more than just one judge

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think the outcome of the Varma case will set a precedent for? Judicial accountability Procedural reforms in judiciary Parliamentary powers Conflict of interest standards 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: It began with a fire.On the intervening night of March 14-15, 2025, firefighters responding to a blaze at the official residence of Delhi high court judge Yashwant Varma stumbled upon something far more consequential than the fire itself: a large quantity of burnt currency notes in a storeroom.What followed turned into an extraordinary judicial and political saga: an in-house inquiry, Varma’s transfer to the Allahabad high court, a Parliamentary removal motion, his decision to withdraw from the inquiry and, eventually, his resignation as a judge.Now, almost 18 months after that night, a Parliamentary inquiry committee has found the charges against Varma proved, paving the way for the Centre to pursue his impeachment even though he has already resigned.The case raises a question that goes beyond what happened in that storeroom: Why is Parliament still pursuing the removal of a judge who is no longer in office, and what would his impeachment mean for the judiciary?To understand that, it is worth going back to the night when the fire brought the cash to light.A fire was reported at Justice Varma’s residence in the early hours of March 15, 2025. Firefighters were called to douse the blaze.After the fire was brought under control, first responders found a large quantity of cash inside a storeroom. The discovery led to official entries documenting the recovery of what appeared to be unaccounted money.The news of the incident quickly reached then Chief Justice of India Sanjiv Khanna. He called an immediate meeting of the collegium, which unanimously decided to transfer Varma to his parent high court, the Allahabad high court.Khanna also constituted a three-member in-house committee to examine the allegations.It comprised Punjab and Haryana high court Chief Justice Sheel Nagu, Himachal Pradesh high court Chief Justice G S Sandhawalia and Karnataka high court Justice Anu Sivaraman.The committee’s voluminous report concluded that the storeroom was under the control of Varma and his family and recommended steps for his removal.Varma denied the allegations and maintained that he had been framed.“I state unequivocally that no cash was ever placed in that storeroom either by me or any of my family members and strongly denounce the suggestion that the alleged cash belonged to us. The very idea or suggestion that this cash was kept or stored by us is totally preposterous,” he said in his response.The matter did not end with the in-house inquiry.After the in-house committee recommended Varma’s removal, Parliament stepped in.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla received a motion signed by 146 members of the Lower House from both the governing and opposition parties seeking Varma’s removal.Acting on the notice, Birla constituted a three-member committee to inquire into the “grounds for request for removal” under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.Supreme Court judge Justice Aravind Kumar chaired the committee. Its original members were Madras high court Chief Justice Manindra Mohan Shrivastava and senior advocate BV Acharya.Shrivastava was later replaced by Bombay high court Chief Justice Shree Chandrashekhar ahead of his retirement.The inquiry then became a full-fledged legal battle.Varma did not simply accept the proceedings.Through a team of senior lawyers, he filed 11 interim applications, examined the records and cross-examined witnesses produced before the committee.The presenting side concluded its evidence on March 17. The committee then asked Varma to furnish a list of his defence witnesses and their affidavits.He sought additional time and was granted an extension. But the deadline passed without him submitting either the list or the affidavits.On April 9, Varma informed the committee that he would no longer participate in the proceedings.In his communication, he questioned the fairness of the inquiry on several grounds. He objected to the use of material from the earlier in-house inquiry, argued that the burden of proof had effectively been shifted onto him and alleged that crucial witnesses had not been examined.He also raised the issue of missing CCTV footage, arguing that it could have helped settle key questions surrounding the case.A day later, on April 10, Varma resigned as a judge of the Allahabad high court.In his resignation letter to the President, he did not spell out the reasons for his decision, saying he did not wish to burden the “august office” with them.“It is with deep anguish that I tender my resignation as Judge of Allahabad HC with immediate effect,” Varma wrote.But his resignation did not necessarily bring the matter to an end.Almost 18 months after the cash was discovered, a Parliamentary inquiry committee tabled its report in the House on August 12 and found all charges against Varma proved.The committee found that Varma possessed a substantial quantity of currency notes in the storeroom of his official residence at 30, Tughlaq Crescent. It accepted videos showing charred notes as well as the testimonies of several Delhi Fire Services and police officials.The panel also found Varma guilty of tampering with the scene of the incident. According to the report, the storeroom was cleaned by his household staff, after which the notes were no longer available.It further described Varma’s explanation for the discovery of the unaccounted cash as “evasive” and “unsatisfactory”, rejecting his claim that the currency notes had been planted.The findings have now brought the case to another crucial stage: the impeachment process.This is where the Varma case becomes constitutionally unusual.The Centre is likely to initiate the impeachment process in the Winter Session of Parliament, even though Varma has already resigned.According to a PTI report citing sources, his resignation does not affect the proceedings because it was submitted only after the removal process had begun in Parliament.The government’s reported reasoning goes beyond Varma himself. It wants to establish a precedent and send a message that a judge cannot avoid a removal process by resigning after serious irregularities have already been alleged and proceedings have begun.Constitutional lawyer advocate Ajinkya Udane said the case could become significant for future situations involving judges who resign while facing removal proceedings.“The matter may also become significant for future cases involving judges who resign while facing removal proceedings. A clear determination could help establish how similar situations should be dealt with and whether resignation can prevent an already initiated parliamentary process from reaching its conclusion,” Udane told The Times of India.“Resignation and removal through impeachment are legally different situations and may have different consequences for pension and other post-service benefits,” he added.A CBI inquiry has also been discussed as a possible course of action.The removal of a judge is deliberately made difficult by the Constitution.Article 124(4) says a Supreme Court judge can be removed only by an order of the President following an address by each House of Parliament. Such an address must be supported by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of at least two-thirds of members present and voting, in the same session, on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.Article 218 extends the same removal procedure to high court judges.That high threshold explains why impeachment proceedings against judges are rare and why the Varma case could become an important test of how the process works when a judge resigns midway.No judge of a superior court in India has ever been successfully removed through impeachment.There have been several attempts, but each ended before a judge was formally removed, either because the judge resigned or because the motion failed to secure the required majority.The first major case was that of Justice V Ramaswami in 1993. As Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana high court, he faced allegations of extravagant spending on his official residence.A Speaker-appointed inquiry committee found him guilty on 11 of 14 charges. But when the impeachment motion came up for a vote in the Lok Sabha, Congress MPs abstained. The motion consequently failed to secure the required majority.Justice Soumitra Sen came closer in 2011.A Calcutta high court judge, Sen faced allegations of misappropriating funds he had handled years earlier as a court-appointed receiver. The Rajya Sabha became the first House of Parliament to pass an impeachment motion against a judge when it approved the motion against Sen.But Sen resigned before the Lok Sabha could take up the motion, preventing him from becoming the first judge to be formally removed from office.Justice P D Dinakaran, then Chief Justice of the Sikkim high court, faced corruption allegations in 2011 that surfaced while he was being considered for elevation to the Supreme Court.The then Rajya Sabha chairman constituted a three-member inquiry committee, but Dinakaran resigned before the process could be completed, citing a lack of confidence in the committee’s impartiality.Other attempts did not progress as far.In 2015, motions were moved against Justice J B Pardiwala of the Gujarat high court over his remarks on reservation and against Justice S K Gangele of the Madhya Pradesh high court over sexual harassment allegations. Neither case resulted in a functioning inquiry committee or a vote on the floor of Parliament.The Varma case, therefore, is not simply about the allegations surrounding a storeroom at a Delhi residence.It has now become a test of how India’s judicial accountability mechanism works when allegations of serious misconduct are made against a judge, and what happens when that judge resigns after Parliament has already begun the process of examining his removal.For Varma, the Parliamentary committee’s findings represent the latest and potentially most consequential chapter in a saga he has consistently denied.For Parliament and the judiciary, the case could leave behind a question that extends well beyond the individual judge: Can resignation bring an end to accountability proceedings against a judge, or can an impeachment process continue once it has already begun?The answer could shape how similar cases are handled in the future.
Article Summary: Yashwant Varma is likely to be impeached after a Parliamentary panel found all charges against him proved. A fire was reported at Justice Varma’s residence in the early hours of March 15, 2025. After the fire was brought under control, first responders found a large quantity of cash inside a storeroom. The discovery led to official entries documenting the recovery of what appeared to be unaccounted money.

Article Title: Justice Yashwant Varma cash-at-home row: Can Parliament still remove judge from office?
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: There is little chance of the Lok Sabha continuing with Justice Varma’s removal motion despite the inquiry committee finding the charges relating to discovery of unaccounted currency notes in his official residential premises proved.As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the President”. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings, finding the writing on the wall.How does a resignation of a constitutional court judge take effect? This question was answered by a five-judge bench of the SC in the Gopal Chandra Misra case on Feb 15, 1978. It was unanimous that once the judge sends his resignation to the President, he/she is deemed to have ceased to be a judge.In that case, the judge had set a prospective date for his resignation taking effect and before the arrival of the appointed date, he had withdrawn his resignation. SC had by four to one majority ruled that since the resignation was prospective, the judge had every right to withdraw it prior to the appointed date.
Article Summary: Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings. As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the President’

Article Title: Ready for long debate, can answer any question but opposition doesn’t want it: Amit Shah
Article Text:

BJP

accuses Rahul of ‘anti-democracy, anarchic’ mindset

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday flung a challenge at the opposition for a comprehensive debate over police action during the anti-NEET protests in Delhi on July 20, saying he was ready for a 24-hour-long debate in Parliament at an hour’s notice over their charge of police excesses against protesting students. He said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him.“If they give their consent for discussion to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla at 2 pm, a debate can begin at 3 pm and go on till 3 pm the next day. I am ready to answer any question. But they (opposition) do not want debate to take place in Parliament. Let the people decide who is running away,” he told the media a day before the end of the monsoon session, which has been marred by the opposition’s disruptions over a host of issues. Soon after, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said govt could even push for the session’s extension if the opposition wants.Shah said while the opposition had initially demanded his statement, govt had gone beyond it by agreeing to an extensive debate followed by his reply so that people could decide who was right and who was wrong.Amit Shah’s aggressive counter was seconded by a host of senior BJP functionaries, with party president Nitin Nabin saying the conduct of Rahul and the entire opposition was reflective of their “anarchic and anti-democracy” mindset.“The entire session is about to be over but they did not agree to a serious discussion over any issue,” he said, accusing them of running away after govt’s offer of a debate.With INDIA bloc MPs frequently accusing him of “running away” from Parliament, Shah hit back and said he was regularly in his chamber in the House. When the opposition was not letting the House function, what was the point of him going there, he asked.Expressing anguish at his opponents’ jibes like “lapata” (missing) and “bhagora” (fugitive) for him, Shah said these terms were being used only recently in parliamentary discourse.The minister later wrote to the Speaker, urging him to reach out to the opposition so that a discussion could begin. “You can allot as much time you think appropriate with mutual agreement. I want to participate in the discussion and I’m ready to answer every question of the opposition,” he said, adding that a solution to any issue in democracy emerged from dialogue and discussion.Congress had normalised disruption in Parliament, he said, adding a party which governed India for decades had fallen to such a low that it did not want discussion in the House.
Article Summary: Amit Shah said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him. He said if they give their consent for discussion to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla at 2 pm, a debate can begin at 3 pm and go on till 3 pm the next day.

Article Title: How a 37-year-old Von Miller with 138.5 career sacks plans to haunt quarterbacks one more time? This time for America's Team
Article Text:
Von Miller signs with Cowboys (Getty Images)

Can Von Miller still get to the quarterback at 37?

What does Von Miller's signing mean for the Cowboys' pass rush in 2026?

Why did Von Miller choose the Dallas Cowboys over other teams?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Von Miller spent weeks working out near The Star in Frisco, posting photoshopped images of himself in a Cowboys uniform and dropping hints that Dallas was where he wanted to be. On Sunday night, it became official. The 37-year-old pass rusher, who leads all active NFL players with 138.5 career sacks, agreed to a one-year deal with the Dallas Cowboys, completing a homecoming years in the making. Miller grew up in DeSoto, Texas, just 30 minutes from AT&T Stadium, and attended Texas A&M before becoming one of the most feared edge rushers in NFL history.The short answer is yes. And last season gave every reason to believe it.With the Washington Commanders in 2025, Von Miller posted nine sacks across 17 games while starting just three and playing only 37 percent of the defensive snaps. Nine sacks from 420 snaps. That production rate would turn heads from a player half his age. For Miller at 36, it was a reminder that his instincts and technique still work when his body is fresh. He is no longer an every-down defender, and the Cowboys are not expecting him to be one. But as a situational pass rusher who picks his spots, he still has the tools to make quarterbacks uncomfortable.The numbers behind his career tell a bigger story. Miller's 138.5 sacks put him tied with Hall of Famer and former Cowboy DeMarcus Ware for ninth in NFL history.Just four more sacks in Dallas would move him past Terrell Suggs, Jason Taylor, and Michael Strahan into sixth all-time. At his snap rate from last season, that milestone is well within reach. In the playoffs, he has 10.5 sacks across 16 career games, the most among any active player. The big moments have never intimidated him.Miller confirmed the news Sunday night on social media, posting a picture of himself in a Cowboys uniform with the caption: "Dallas! Let's make this one Special."Dallas already had one of the more intriguing edge units heading into the season. Rashan Gary, acquired in a trade from Green Bay, brings athleticism and proven production. Donovan Ezeiruaku, a second-round pick in 2025, showed flashes of something real in his rookie year. First-round rookie Malachi Lawrence is a player this coaching staff believes in. Now they get Miller too.Defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who briefly overlapped with Miller in Denver in 2021, knows what this signing is and is not. It is not a plug-and-play starter. It is a chess piece. Parker spoke about his young linebacker group at training camp in June with genuine confidence: "It's a younger group, but it's a hungry group. I think we're going to have the play style that we want. Those guys want to be held accountable. They want to be responsible for stopping the run and affecting the quarterback, and we'll be able to do that."Adding Miller to that room does not crowd those younger players out. If anything, it accelerates their development. Having a two-time Super Bowl champion, an eight-time Pro Bowl selection, and the active sack leader showing up every day is not a roadblock for Ezeiruaku or Lawrence. It is a masterclass. The Cowboys are not just signing a rotational pass rusher. They are putting a future Hall of Famer in a mentorship role with their most important young defenders.This was not purely a business decision. Von Miller had options. He enters his 15th season as one of the most decorated pass rushers in the game, and teams around the league were aware of what he showed in Washington. But from the moment he started training near The Star this summer, the message was clear: he wanted to come home.Miller's path to Dallas was not a straight line. He won his first Super Bowl with the Broncos in 2016, earning MVP honors. A half-season stint with the Rams brought a second ring in 2022. Then came three seasons with the Buffalo Bills, interrupted by a torn ACL that cost him significant time in 2022 and 2023. Washington gave him a fresh start in 2025, and he delivered. Now, after five teams and 14 seasons, he gets to play professional football in the state where he grew up, for the team his region has always followed.The Cowboys open their 2026 season against the New York Giants on Sunday Night Football. It is a stage Miller has performed on many times before. For Dallas, a team carrying real playoff ambitions this year, having a proven pass rusher who can win in key moments is exactly the kind of low-risk, high-upside addition that smart rosters are built on. The price is modest. The potential return is not.
Article Summary: Von Miller signs a one-year deal with the Dallas Cowboys. The 37-year-old pass rusher leads all active NFL players with 138.5 career sacks. Miller grew up in DeSoto, Texas, and attended Texas A&M before becoming one of the most feared edge rushers.

Article Title: Why Brittany Mahomes' "relatively uncommon" back injury recovery story is quietly becoming one of the most inspiring in sports
Article Text:
Brittany Mahomes' back injury recovery story (Instagram)

What caused Brittany Mahomes' back injury and how serious was it?

How did Brittany Mahomes recover from her back injury, and what can other women learn from it?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Most people know Brittany Mahomes as Patrick Mahomes ' wife, the Kansas City Current co-owner, or the loudest voice in any Chiefs stadium suite. What rarely gets the same airtime is the fact that she spent nearly two years rebuilding her body after fracturing her back, a postpartum injury she kept mostly to herself while simultaneously managing three kids, a fitness brand, and a professional sports franchise. By early 2026, she was back squatting 70 lbs in a gym without pain. That kind of recovery does not happen overnight, and the road there was far messier than a few Instagram Stories let on.In March 2024, Brittany Mahomes posted a note on her Instagram Stories that was short, blunt, and caught a lot of people off guard. "Just your daily reminder: Once you have kids please take care of your pelvic floor. Seriously," she wrote. Then the sign-off: "From: A girl with a fractured back."There were no dramatic announcements. No long captions about her struggle. Just a quiet warning to other mothers and a small window into what she had been dealing with privately. The injury stemmed from pelvic floor issues after two pregnancies. She had initially tried to train at her pre-pregnancy intensity until her body gave out.According to ob/gyn Dr. Yves-Richard Dole, Brittany's injury is "relatively uncommon."The pelvic floor is connected to the lower back, and each of the bones are connected together by a series of ligaments and tissue. When those muscles weaken after childbirth and are not given adequate recovery time, the structural load on the spine can shift in ways that lead to stress fractures.She then committed to pelvic floor therapy, chiropractic care, and X-rays to work her way back. None of it was fast. By August 2024, while pregnant with her third child, she managed her first back squat in over a year. Five months later, her fitness coach Kristy Rae shared a video of Brittany squatting 70 lbs, writing: "A year and a half ago, rehabbing a broken back meant severe pain and limited movement. Now, almost a year postpartum and progressively getting stronger every week. Proof that the body is capable of incredible things when you meet it with patience and intentional training."The recovery was not linear. Brittany Mahomes had a third pregnancy running parallel to the rehabilitation, which meant her body was healing and changing at the same time. That is a genuinely complicated medical situation, not simply a matter of rest and willpower.By March 2026, nearly two years after going public with the injury, she shared that she can now perform heavy deadlifts again, without pain. She wrote: "Never thought I would see the day of doing (kinda heavy) deadlifts again with no pain. Man they felt good." That single line carried a lot of weight, not because of the exercise itself, but because of everything it took to get there.What makes Brittany's story worth paying attention to is less about celebrity and more about context. Pelvic floor injuries after childbirth are underreported and rarely discussed openly in sports culture. Brittany's experience, shared across a platform of millions, brought an unglamorous but important women's health issue into a sports conversation that does not typically make room for it.Now, with Patrick recovering from his own ACL and MCL tear heading into the 2026 season, there is a strange symmetry at Arrowhead. Two elite competitors under the same roof, both working back from serious injuries, both choosing patience over a rushed return. Brittany has already been through the other side of that tunnel. That is not a footnote to Patrick's story. It is its own.
Article Summary: Brittany Mahomes fractured her back while pregnant with her third child. By early 2026, she was back squatting 70 lbs in a gym without pain. The injury stemmed from pelvic floor issues after two pregnancies. Brittany's experience brought an unglamorous but important women's health issue into a sports conversation that does not typically make room for it.

Now, with a championship ring from New York and a wedding ring for Jordyn Woods, the two are entering 2026 as one of sports and entertainment's more scrutinized power couples financially.Towns' individual net worth sits at roughly $100 million, per Celebrity Net Worth. The bulk of it traces back to basketball. Minnesota took him first overall in the 2015 draft after a single, defense-first season at Kentucky under John Calipari, and he answered by averaging 18.3 points and 10.5 rebounds as a rookie, good enough for a unanimous Rookie of the Year vote.The money followed the production. His rookie deal was worth $25.7 million over four years, but a 2018 max extension bumped that to $190 million over five years. Minnesota went bigger in 2022, locking him into a four-year, $224 million supermax that averages $56 million annually and can climb past $270 million with incentives, among the richest annual salaries in NBA history at signing. Endorsements with Nike, Gatorade, Beats by Dre, and Panini add another layer on top of the on-court earnings.Towns now plays for the New York Knicks, with whom he won a title in the 2025-26 season.Woods' path ran through a different industry entirely. Born in Los Angeles in 1997, she signed with Wilhelmina in 2015 after being scouted on Instagram, and her profile grew fast through her friendship with Kylie Jenner, culminating in the 2017 E! series "Life of Kylie." Television and modeling work followed: multiple "Keeping Up with the Kardashians" appearances, a "Grown-ish" guest role, a stint on "The Masked Singer" as Kangaroo, and a "Red Table Talk" appearance.Business became her bigger play. Her SECNDNTURE activewear line launched in 2018, followed by a Boohoo collaboration, an Easilocks hair extensions line, a PrettyLittleThing capsule, and her own fitness brand, FRSTPLACE. Celebrity Net Worth puts her fortune at around $6 million, a fraction of Towns' figure, but built almost entirely outside of sports, which is part of what makes the pairing financially unusual.On the giving side, Towns runs the Karl-Anthony Towns Foundation, which funds education, healthcare, and community programs. He ramped up donations to COVID-19 relief efforts in New Jersey and Minnesota after losing his mother to the virus in 2020, and he's partnered with the Timberwolves organization on scholarships and youth initiatives.Woods, meanwhile, moved into a rented Los Angeles home in 2020 after her split from the Kardashian-Jenner circle, a property with multiple bedrooms, a custom kitchen, an arcade room, and floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the mountains. Real estate specifics on their post-wedding living situation haven't been detailed publicly.The two started dating in May 2020, not long after Woods' well-documented fallout with the Kardashian-Jenner family. Their wedding drew a heavily star-studded guest list, including Justin and Hailey Bieber, Kylie Jenner, Timothée Chalamet, Ben Stiller, Teyana Taylor, and Michael B. Jordan, alongside several of Towns' NBA teammates. Guests reportedly received custom "Married in 15" hoodies and Fanatics gift bags as they left the reception.For Towns, it caps a decade that took him from a top overall pick to a champion, a max-contract cornerstone, and now a newlywed, with a financial partnership that's just getting started.
Article Summary: Karl-Anthony Towns and Jordyn Woods are one of sports and entertainment's more scrutinized power couples financially. Towns' individual net worth sits at roughly $100 million, per Celebrity Net Worth. Woods' net worth is estimated at around $6 million, but built almost entirely outside of sports.

Article Title: Did Jake Paul call off his Jutta Leerdam wedding? The truth behind viral ‘cheating’ claims
Article Text:
Did Jake Paul call off his Jutta Leerdam wedding? The truth behind viral ‘cheating’ claims

Is Jake Paul and Jutta Leerdam’s wedding really called off?

What has Jake Paul said about Jutta Leerdam’s breakup rumors?

A viral X post claiming Jake Paul has called off his wedding to Jutta Leerdam over cheating and high spending is false. The August 14 post from @ipostrandom21 uses an older clip of Paul and adds made-up captions that make it appear he is discussing a breakup. The post claims Paul said Leerdam cheated three times, that he begged her to stay and that he spent $100,000 a month on her. None of those claims is backed by a credible interview, podcast, post or report. Recent evidence instead shows Paul and Leerdam are still engaged and preparing for their wedding.The viral post says: “Jake Paul CALLS OFF his wedding to Jutta Leerdam after claiming she cheated on him three more times, admitting he used to beg her to stay and was spending $100K A MONTH on her before finally reaching his breaking point. 😳”It then adds two supposed quotes: “I told her after the third one I’m done.” and “She thought I was joking.”There is no evidence that Jake Paul said either line. The video does not show him discussing cheating, a cancelled wedding or money spent on Leerdam. Instead, it is older podcast-style footage that has been given a new story through text added over the video.That matters because similar posts about the couple have appeared before, using old footage and dramatic claims to attract clicks.An earlier Times of India fact-check found the same pattern of recycled footage. A previous viral video falsely suggested Paul was breaking down over Leerdam, even though the clip did not mention her or their relationship.Paul and Leerdam announced their engagement in March 2025. At the time, Paul wrote, “We’re engaged. We can’t wait to spend forever together.” Their relationship has also been seen publicly since then, including at the 2026 Winter Olympics, where Paul watched Leerdam win gold in the 1,000m.The latest public information also does not match the idea that the wedding has been called off. PEOPLE reported in July that Leerdam was discussing wedding plans and said her must-have for the ceremony was to “Have fun and dance.” She also spoke about the couple enjoying date nights and supporting each other’s goals.The couple did face breakup rumors in April 2026. Paul directly addressed those reports on X, writing: “Seeing the Dutch media lying about my fiancé Jutta and I. There is so much false information being spread about Jutta in the past years. It needs to stop.”That statement does not prove every detail of their private relationship, but it is important when compared with the new viral post. There is still no credible evidence for the specific claims about repeated cheating, a $100,000 monthly spend or a cancelled wedding.The claim therefore rests on an old video and captions that were added later. Until Jake Paul, Leerdam or a credible source provides evidence of a breakup, the viral story should not be treated as a real account of their relationship.
Article Summary: A viral X post claiming Jake Paul has called off his wedding to Jutta Leerdam over cheating and high spending is false. The August 14 post from @ipostrandom21 uses an older clip of Paul and adds made-up captions that make it appear he is discussing a breakup. There is still no credible evidence for the claims about repeated cheating, a $100,000 monthly spend or a cancelled wedding.

Article Title: Inspiring story on motherhood: “Once I had my first child, I didn’t want to leave his side”- How Chris Evert found a deeper kind of happiness after becoming a mother
Article Text:
Inspiring story on motherhood: “Once I had my first child, I didn’t want to leave his side”- How Chris Evert found a deeper kind of happiness after becoming a mother

Why Chris Evert did not want to leave her first child’s side

Los Angeles Times

How Alexander James changed Chris Evert’s view of motherhood

Why Chris Evert’s words still matter years later

We Are Tennis

For Chris Evert, becoming a mother changed what she wanted from life. The tennis great had already walked away from professional tennis when she welcomed her first son, Alexander James, in 1991. But motherhood gave her a feeling that went far beyond retirement. Evert has said, “Once I had my first child, I didn’t want to leave his side.” The simple line explains why her first child quickly became more important than the sport that had defined her for years.Evert became a mother on October 12, 1991, when she and her then husband, former Olympic skier Andy Mill, welcomed Alexander James Mill. She was 36 at the time and had retired from professional tennis two years earlier.Even though Evert was no longer playing full time, tennis had not completely disappeared from her life. She had worked in broadcasting after retirement and had considered taking part in team tennis and exhibition matches. Then Alexander was born, and her plans changed.In a 1992 interview with the, Evert spoke openly about the effect her baby had on her. She said she had thought about returning to the sport while she was pregnant.But after holding Alexander in the hospital, those thoughts disappeared.“I held the baby in the hospital and after the first minute, all those feelings were gone,” Evert said.That helps explain the meaning behind her later comment about not wanting to leave his side. She had spent most of her life preparing for matches, traveling for tournaments and dealing with the pressure that came with being one of the best players in the world. Now, she had a baby who depended on her, and being there with him felt more important.The change was not about suddenly disliking tennis. Evert had simply found something that meant more to her at that stage of her life.Alexander was not just Evert’s first child. His arrival gave her a new way to measure what mattered.Before becoming a mother, much of Evert’s public life centered on tennis. She won 18 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years near the top of the sport. Winning was a huge part of her identity. Motherhood gave her a role where there was no ranking, trophy or scoreboard.Thereported in 1991 that Evert compared winning Wimbledon with having a baby. Her view was striking. A major title could bring happiness and recognition, but the feeling did not last in the same way. Having her child was something she could hold on to.“The great high of winning Wimbledon lasts for about a week,” Evert told, according to the. “But having a baby, there just isn’t any comparison.”Her words show why the birth of Alexander was such a turning point. Evert had already achieved the biggest goals in tennis. She did not need another trophy to prove what she could do. Instead, she wanted to enjoy the new part of her life that had arrived.That did not mean she stopped being Chris Evert the tennis champion. It meant she had become Chris Evert the mother too, and she was learning that the second role could bring a different kind of happiness.Alexander was the first of Evert and Andy Mill’s three sons. Nicholas was born in 1994, followed by Colton in 1996. Together, the boys became the center of a busy family life.Evert later made it clear that her feelings about motherhood had not faded as her children grew. In a 2001 interview with the, she spoke about Alexander, Nicholas and Colton while they were still young.“They’re my life, they’re the most important thing,” Evert said. “I’m busy, but I’m 100 percent a mom first.”That comment adds another layer to her earlier quote. Evert was not talking only about the excitement of having her first baby. She was describing a lasting change in how she saw herself.Her sons also grew up around sports because both of their parents were successful athletes. Still, Evert did not push them to follow the same path she had taken. She wanted them to enjoy being children instead of feeling that they had to become champions.In a later interview with, Evert again placed motherhood above her tennis achievements. Asked about the best part of being Chris Evert, she immediately pointed to her sons and being a mother.“I love my boys,” she said. “That’s been the highlight of my life.”That answer is important because it came decades after Alexander was born. Her feelings were not limited to those first few months of motherhood. They remained part of how Evert viewed her life long after her playing career had ended.Evert’s quote is simple, but it says something many parents can understand. Having a child can change what feels urgent. Things that once seemed extremely important can suddenly move down the list.For Evert, that shift came after years of living with the demands of professional tennis. She had known what it meant to spend months traveling and competing. She had also known the feeling of winning major titles in front of huge crowds.Yet when Alexander arrived, she wanted to stay close to him.That decision did not erase tennis from her life. Evert later worked as a coach, mentor and commentator, and she remained connected to the sport she had helped shape. But her relationship with tennis was different because she no longer needed to prove herself through competition.Her three sons became the part of her life she spoke about with the most pride. In 2025,again asked her about the best thing about being Chris Evert. Her answer centered on being a mother.That is why the line, “Once I had my first child, I didn’t want to leave his side,” carries more meaning than it may seem to at first. Evert was not simply describing a mother wanting to stay with her newborn. She was describing the moment her priorities changed.For a woman who had spent decades being defined by tennis, motherhood became the part of her identity she valued most. And for Evert, that change began with one child, Alexander, and the feeling that nothing else mattered quite as much as being beside him.
Article Summary: Evert became a mother on October 12, 1991, when she and her then husband, former Olympic skier Andy Mill, welcomed Alexander James Mill. The tennis great had already walked away from professional tennis when she welcomed her first son, Alexander James, in 1991. Evert later made it clear that her feelings about motherhood had not faded as her children grew up.

Article Title: India vs England: Craig Fulton’s young side chases first World Cup win over England since 1994
Article Text:
Amstelveen, Aug 16 (IANS) The Indian men's hockey team will look to build on its winning start to the FIH Hockey World Cup 2026 when it takes on England in its second Pool D match at the Wagener Hockey Stadium here on Monday.

In the current men’s hockey team, if one looks for players born before 1994, you will find only two — Manpreet Singh and Amit Rohidas. A young side, barring the two veterans, none of the others were even born the last time India defeated England in a World Cup contest. Monday’s meeting then must count as a unique first.That victory came at the 1994 edition in Sydney, when Mohammad Riaz scored the winner as India finished sixth. Since then, India have endured three defeats — often in close contests — against England in World Cups. Their best result came in the previous edition in Bhubaneswar, where the teams played out a goalless draw.This is a record Craig Fulton’s side will be keen to set straight when they face the world No. 3 side on Monday. India have, however, ticked a few boxes against England in recent times, the biggest being their quarterfinal victory at the Paris Olympics.India opened their World Cup campaign with a 3-1 victory over Wales on Saturday, while England defeated Pakistan 4-1.India could afford moments of sluggishness against Wales, but England will present a different challenge. One of the biggest positives from the opener was the coordination between the strike force and midfield.The biggest concern was the drop in intensity during the final 10 minutes. “Since we have started playing the Pro League, it’s been pretty equal. But the World Cup is different. It’s a must-win game for both the teams. They are the highest-ranked team in our pool, so we are really going to go after them,” he said.

Article Title: 'There is pressure': PV Sindhu eyes historic sixth World Championships medal on home soil

PV Sindhu ahead of BWF World Championship on home soil (ANI Image)

“I won’t deny that there is no pressure. There is pressure.” For PV Sindhu , however, pressure and purpose can coexist.As she returns to the BWF World Championships on home soil, the two-time Olympic medallist is chasing a historic sixth medal, while insisting the hunger that has driven her since her senior career began at 14 remains undiminished.Sindhu owns five Worlds medals — bronze in 2013 and 2014, silver in 2017 and 2018, and gold in 2019.A sixth would make her the first player in the championship’s history to reach that mark, moving past China’s Lin Dan and Zhao Yunlei, who also collected five.“Having five medals at the World Championships is an amazing journey, and each medal gave me a different kind of experience,” Sindhu said here on Sunday. “The hunger towards the game hasn’t changed, and I definitely know it’s in me. I can still do it.” Seven years after her golden run, she is determined to return to the podium.“Winning the Japan Open gave me a lot of confidence and a lot of boost,” Sindhu said. “I hope I keep the same confidence. Everything is going well.” The title ended a nearly two-year wait for a major crown and offered timely evidence that her game, movement and belief are heading in the right direction now.“I have had the sports science, the physio and the trainer. We all came together, sat down and noted what is required.It’s not just the tournaments; it’s behind the scenes, what we do, what is required, and how smartly we adapt.” Metrics, recovery and careful load management, she said, are helping her peak at the right time.That preparation has also sharpened her mental conditioning. “Physically and mentally it has been quite good. I am able to see the changes in terms of my game and my movement. I am happy it is going in the right way,” she said.The journey began in 2009, when a young Sindhu watched the Worlds in Hyderabad “from morning until evening”. “Back then, I didn’t know how serious it was,” she recalled.“Now I look back and realise I got to experience the best. The whole journey has been quite memorable.”Now, with the championships returning to India after 17 years, Sindhu is happy with the arrangements.“I really appreciate their effort for doing it. Here the conditions and everything...the way they have changed is really good,” she said.

Article Title: João Cancelo set to sign permanently for Barcelona on Tuesday as free agent after Al Hilal contract termination
Article Text:
João Cancelo is set to return to Barcelona on a free transfer after terminating his Al Hilal contract/ Instagram

Cancelo finally gets the permanent Barcelona move

A third arrival, but a first permanent signing

Barcelona's summer plans gather pace

João Cancelo is set to return to Barcelona for a third spell after reaching an agreement to terminate his contract with Al Hilal, clearing the way for the Portugal international to rejoin the Spanish champions as a free agent.The 32-year-old had one year remaining on his contract in Saudi Arabia, but his desire to return to Barcelona has now been matched by an agreement that allows him to leave without a transfer fee. He is expected in Barcelona on Tuesday to complete the move and sign his contract.Cancelo had already agreed personal terms with Barcelona in June, with the remaining obstacle being his situation at Al Hilal. That has now been resolved after the player and Saudi club reached an agreement on an early termination.According to sources cited by ESPN, Cancelo will join Barcelona as a free agent after previously spending two loan spells at the club. He first arrived from Manchester City for the 2023-24 season before returning to Al Hilal, then came back to Barcelona on loan during the second half of last season.That second spell proved important. Cancelo helped Barcelona win LaLiga and made it clear that he wanted to remain at the club permanently.The situation had appeared difficult because Al Hilal had initially valued him at around €10 million, before reportedly raising their asking price to €15 million. Barcelona's preference was to avoid a significant transfer fee, and the eventual termination of Cancelo's Saudi contract has removed that obstacle.He is now set to make the move without Barcelona having to negotiate a transfer fee with Al Hilal.This will technically be Cancelo's third time signing for Barcelona, although it will be the first occasion on which he joins on a permanent contract.His first spell began in August 2023, when Barcelona signed him on loan from Manchester City for the 2023-24 campaign. Financial limitations meant they could not turn that arrangement into a permanent transfer, and Cancelo subsequently moved from City to Al Hilal.He returned to Barcelona in January 2026 on another six-month loan from the Saudi club and helped the team secure the LaLiga title.The Portugal international has now secured the permanent return he had been seeking.Before reaching the top level with Manchester City and Barcelona, Cancelo came through at Benfica and also played for Valencia, Inter Milan and Juventus. He spent part of 2023 on loan at Bayern Munich before joining Al Hilal in 2024.His honours include league titles in Portugal, England, Italy, Germany and Spain, making him the first player this century to win the top-flight title in four of Europe's five major leagues.Cancelo becomes Barcelona's fourth signing of the summer, following Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi and Jesse Bisiwu.The club's recruitment has continued to develop rapidly, with Rodri also reportedly agreeing a €76.5 million ($88.4 million) move from Manchester City on the same day. That would reunite Cancelo with his former City team-mate in a Barcelona squad that has already retained the Spanish league title and is looking to strengthen further.Barcelona are also pursuing a striker, with Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez reported to be their preferred target, while another No. 9 and potentially a centre-back remain under consideration.After Sunday's 5-2 friendly victory over Basel, manager Hansi Flick acknowledged that more business could still take place.“We will see what happens, but it could be that we are still lacking something,” Flick said.For Cancelo, however, the uncertainty is largely over. After two temporary stays in Catalonia and an increasingly complicated spell in Saudi Arabia, he is now expected to return to Barcelona on Tuesday with the opportunity to finally make the Camp Nou his permanent home.
Article Summary: João Cancelo is set to return to Barcelona on a free transfer. Portugal international has reached an agreement to terminate his contract with Al Hilal. The 32-year-old had one year remaining on his contract in Saudi Arabia. He is expected in Barcelona on Tuesday to complete the move and sign his contract.

Article Title: Barcelona finally get Ballon d’Or winner Rodri after third offer as Man City reportedly accept €76.5m deal
Article Text:
Spain's Rodri celebrates with the tournament's best player award after the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Abbie Parr)

Barcelona return with third offer

A statement signing for Barcelona

Rodri leaves City after seven seasons

Rodri with the 2024 Ballon d'Or trophy

City prepare for life without their midfield anchor

Barcelona have reportedly reached an agreement in principle to sign Rodri from Manchester City, with the Spain captain set to return to La Liga after seven trophy-filled seasons in England.The proposed deal is understood to be worth €76.5 million (about $88.4 million) in total, after Barcelona returned with a third offer for the 30-year-old midfielder. Rodri is set to sign a four-year contract with the La Liga champions. The move would bring one of the world's most accomplished midfielders back to Spain just weeks after he captained the country to the 2026 World Cup and was named the tournament's best player.Barcelona had already seen two approaches for Rodri rejected before returning with an improved proposal over the weekend.According to sources cited by ESPN and The Athletic , Barcelona’s third offer takes the total package to €76.5 million ($88.4m). City will receive an upfront €60 million ($68.8m), with more than €11 million in highly achievable bonuses, and the Premier League club expects to receive at least €71.5 million overall for Rodri, who has less than 12 months left on his contract.Rodri is expected to travel to Barcelona in the coming days and could be presented before Wednesday's Joan Gamper Trophy match against Al Ahly at Spotify Camp Nou.The agreement follows a summer in which Rodri's future had become increasingly uncertain. He was entering the final year of his Manchester City contract, giving the English club a reason to consider a sale if the right offer arrived.Barcelona's interest also developed after Frenkie de Jong suffered a long-term injury, prompting the Spanish champions to explore the midfield market more seriously.Rodri was not initially considered a priority target, but his availability changed the picture. Barcelona then moved ahead with their pursuit, while sources told ESPN that the midfielder preferred a return to Spain with Barça over a move to Real Madrid.Barcelona see Rodri as a major addition to a squad that has won consecutive Spanish league titles and are understood to view him as a player capable of strengthening Hansi Flick's side for the coming seasons.His arrival would also add another established leader to a summer recruitment drive that has already brought Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi and Jesse Bisiwu to the club.João Cancelo is also set to return to Barcelona as a free agent, according to sources cited by ESPN, while the club continue to pursue a striker. Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez is their leading target following the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.Rodri's experience would be particularly valuable in a squad preparing to compete on multiple fronts. He has won at the highest level in both club and international football, while his ability to control games from midfield has made him one of the defining players in his position.Rodri joined Manchester City from Atlético Madrid in 2019 after previously playing for Villarreal and Atlético.Across 298 appearances in seven seasons, he helped City win 12 major honours, including four Premier League titles, two FA Cups, three EFL Cups and the Champions League in 2022-23.His time in England was interrupted by a serious knee injury that ruled him out for much of the 2024-25 campaign, while a hamstring problem also disrupted parts of last season.He returned to his best level at the 2026 World Cup, captaining Spain to the title after a 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina. Rodri was also awarded the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player.The World Cup triumph followed his success at Euro 2024, where he was also named player of the tournament. That performance helped him win the 2024 Ballon d'Or.Rodri would therefore leave Manchester City having added almost every major honour available to his collection.Barcelona's opening proposal was reportedly rejected last week, with City turning down an offer worth around €45.2 million ($52.2 million) before the Catalan club increased its bid.After Sunday's Community Shield defeat by Arsenal, new City manager Enzo Maresca acknowledged the difficulty of replacing a player of Rodri's calibre.“Rodri is a player who just won the World Cup and Ballon d'Or,” Maresca said. “He's a top player, all the teams need a Rodri, so it's not about if we miss Rodri or not.”Rodri's departure would bring an end to his seven-year spell at the Etihad and leave City without a midfielder who has been central to their most successful period.For Barcelona, meanwhile, the agreement would bring home a player who has already won a World Cup, European Championship and Ballon d'Or, while still being 30 years old and entering what could be several important seasons at the Camp Nou.
Article Summary: Barcelona have reportedly reached an agreement in principle to sign Rodri from Manchester City. The proposed deal is understood to be worth €76.5 million (about $88.4 million) Rodri is set to sign a four-year contract with the La Liga champions. The move would bring one of the world's most accomplished midfielders back to Spain.

Rice took his turn in front of the Arsenal supporters and raised the shield above his head.The moment quickly went wrong.As Rice held the trophy aloft, its stand fell backwards and struck him in the face. The England international initially appeared shocked, but immediately saw the funny side and began laughing before turning towards his team-mates.The incident provided one of the lighter moments of an afternoon dominated by Arsenal's performance.The victory gave Rice his second Community Shield triumph, having also lifted the trophy with Arsenal in 2023.That match also came against Manchester City. Arsenal drew 1-1 at Wembley before winning 4-1 on penalties, giving Rice his first success in the competition.He was one of several midfield options used by Mikel Arteta in Cardiff, alongside Guimarães, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Zubimendi.Arteta later praised the strength of his midfield options when speaking to TNT Sports.“Very strong. I think we have been adding year after year. Quality combinations. Now we have a lot of leadership,” the Arsenal manager said.Rice's trophy mishap came after Arsenal had produced a commanding display against the reigning FA Cup winners.Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring after just 24 seconds, with Lewis-Skelly finding him with a disguised pass. The finish was recorded as the fastest goal in Community Shield history.Kai Havertz doubled Arsenal's advantage in the 28th minute after Christos Tzolis supplied the cross, before Ødegaard completed the 3-0 victory three minutes into the second half.The result gave Arsenal an ideal start to their first campaign as defending Premier League champions after ending their 22-year wait for the title last season.They will now attempt to become only the second team in 16 years to win the Community Shield and Premier League in the same season. Manchester City are the only side to have managed that during the period, doing so after winning the Shield in 2018 before claiming the Premier League title in 2018-19.Arsenal's title last season was their first since 2004 and their 14th overall. They have not won consecutive league titles for 81 years, having last achieved that feat during a three-season run between 1932 and 1935.

Cristiano Ronaldo has said the 2026-27 season could be the final year of his playing career, offering his clearest indication yet that retirement is approaching. The 41-year-old has spent more than two decades at the highest level and, with his contract at Al Nassr running until June 2027, has now begun speaking openly about what he wants his life to look like once football is over.“This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy,” Ronaldo told Vogue in an interview published on Sunday.Ronaldo has previously spoken about retirement without committing to a particular date. In November, he said he expected to continue playing for “one or two years” and confirmed that the 2026 World Cup would be his final tournament.Portugal were eliminated by Spain in the round of 16 last month. Ronaldo scored three goals at the tournament and became the first player to score at six different World Cups, finishing his World Cup career with 11 goals from 27 appearances.He was less specific about his overall playing future after Portugal's exit. His comments toare the closest he has come to putting a timeframe on it.Ronaldo said he has already planned for the period after football and expects to spend more time with his family, travel and play and watch padel.“I have my future all mapped out,” he said. “I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard.“Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one. And also have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I've earned -- what we've earned.“Because after all it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice.”Ronaldo remains contracted to Al Nassr until June 2027 and has continued to play for Portugal after the World Cup.He is also 24 senior goals short of reaching 1,000, a milestone he has spoken about wanting to achieve during the latter stages of his career.Portugal's new manager, Jorge Jesus, described Ronaldo as a “symbol of Portuguese football” after taking the job in July and said he would continue selecting him while the forward remains fit and playing.Ronaldo's three goals at the 2026 World Cup took his international total to 146, the highest in men's international football.His club career has continued alongside those international records. He began at Sporting CP before moving to Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus and Al Nassr. His most prolific spell came in Madrid, where he scored 450 goals in 438 appearances, becoming the club's all-time leading scorer.Ronaldo has won five Ballon d'Ors and five Champions League titles, along with league championships in England, Spain and Italy. With Portugal, he won the European Championship and Nations League.His career has also produced records across club and international football, including his position as men's international football's leading goalscorer and his six World Cup appearances.The 2026 tournament was already established as the end of his World Cup career. Now, with the new domestic season beginning, Ronaldo has indicated that the wider playing career could have only one more season left.His comments came in an interview conducted five days before his marriage to Georgina Rodríguez in Cascais, Portugal. The couple had been together for nearly a decade before announcing their marriage with a photograph of their wedding rings.Ronaldo has also spoken about wanting to spend more time with his family after football and about the interests he intends to pursue away from the sport.Ronaldo's comments came shortly after Lionel Messi expressed uncertainty over how much longer he would continue playing following the death of his father, Jorge.The pair have spent much of the past two decades at the centre of football's defining individual rivalry, collecting major individual awards and setting scoring records while playing for Barcelona, Real Madrid and their respective national teams.Both are now 39 or older, with Ronaldo at 41 and Messi at 39, and both have recently spoken about circumstances that could bring their playing careers towards an end.For Ronaldo, there is still football to play, goals to chase and a contract that extends into 2027. But for the first time, he has put the possibility of retirement at the end of the current season into his own words.

Article Text:

What happened to MLB legend Tommy John before his death?

What was Tommy John known for during his MLB career?

Tommy John, the MLB pitcher whose remarkable return from a serious elbow injury changed baseball, has died at 83. He passed away peacefully at his home in Lakewood Ranch, Florida, surrounded by his wife, Cheryl, and family, according to a statement from his agent, Mike Maguire. The news came days after John shared an emotional goodbye message with baseball fans while receiving hospice care at home.Tommy John’s health had become a concern before his death. TMZ Sports reported that the former MLB pitcher had entered hospice care at his home in Florida. John had also revealed in 2024 that he was battling bladder cancer. However, there has been no official confirmation that cancer caused his death. Reports only say that he died peacefully at 83, surrounded by his wife, Cheryl, and other family members.His final public message came through the New York Yankees during Old-Timers’ Day. John was unable to attend the event, but he sent a message thanking the Yankees, his former teammates and the fans who had supported him throughout his career. He also remembered Dr. Frank Jobe, the surgeon who helped save his pitching career.John wrote, “Thanks to Dr. Jobe, who saved my arm & made it possible for me to continue pitching.The message came only days before his death and gave fans a final chance to hear from the baseball great. While his health had worsened enough for him to receive hospice care, the exact cause of death has not been publicly confirmed. That distinction is important, especially because John had previously spoken about his battle with bladder cancer.John died peacefully at his Florida home on August 16, 2026, with his family beside him. His family will hold a private celebration of life in Florida and has asked those wishing to honor him to donate to the Duke University Medical Fund instead of sending flowers.John played 26 seasons in Major League Baseball from 1963 through 1989. He pitched for the Cleveland Indians, Chicago White Sox, Los Angeles Dodgers, New York Yankees, California Angels and Oakland Athletics. He finished his career with 288 wins and a 3.34 ERA.He was also a four-time All-Star, earning selections in 1968, 1978, 1979 and 1980. But the biggest turning point in his career came in 1974, when he suffered a torn ulnar collateral ligament in his pitching elbow while playing for the Los Angeles Dodgers.Dr. Jobe then performed an experimental elbow reconstruction on John. The surgery forced him to miss the 1975 season, but he returned to the mound in 1976.John went on to win 164 games after the operation and continued pitching until 1989. The procedure later became known as Tommy John surgery and became widely used to treat serious UCL injuries in baseball pitchers.That comeback became the biggest part of John’s legacy. His career showed that a pitcher could return from an injury that had once been seen as a possible end to a career. Today, his name remains closely connected to one of baseball’s most important medical procedures.
Article Summary: Tommy John passed away peacefully at his home in Lakewood Ranch, Florida, surrounded by his wife, Cheryl, and family, according to a statement from his agent, Mike Maguire. The news came days after John shared an emotional goodbye message with baseball fans while receiving hospice care at home. John played 26 seasons in Major League Baseball from 1963 through 1989.

Article Title: Super Bowl LXI lands on Valentine’s Day for the first time in history creating an unusual football-versus-romance showdown
Article Text:
Super Bowl LXI (Getty Images)

Super Bowl LXI and Valentine’s Day create a unique clash

Super Bowl 2027 brings another major change for NFL fans

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Super Bowl LXI is about to create a very unusual sporting dilemma. The NFL ’s championship game is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine’s Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. With romance and football competing for the same Sunday, fans have already begun joking about dinner reservations, watch parties and the ultimate relationship compromise.The date alone is enough to make the 2027 Super Bowl stand out. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, meaning couples will have to decide how they want to spend one of the biggest nights on the American sporting calendar.For football fans, the answer may seem obvious. For couples with different priorities, however, the evening could require some negotiation.Social media has already embraced the idea. One Reddit commenter joked about the pressure on restaurants, writing:"The Valentine's Day brunch reservations are going to be harder to get than a Super Bowl ticket."Another post took the joke even further, imagining the holiday as a test of romantic loyalty:"Super Bowl on Valentine's? Peak relationship apocalypse incoming—guys choosing touchdowns over touchy-feely dates. Ladies, demand a halftime proposal or it's single season next year."The humor works because the conflict is so easy to imagine. A romantic dinner could overlap with pregame coverage. A reservation might clash with kickoff.And anyone hosting a Super Bowl party could suddenly find themselves planning around Valentine's Day expectations.There is also a convenient escape route. The game falls on Presidents' Day weekend, giving many people the chance to turn the occasion into a longer celebration. Couples could celebrate Valentine's Day on Saturday, watch the Super Bowl on Sunday and use Monday to recover from the late night.The unusual date is not the only reason Super Bowl LXI will be significant. ESPN will broadcast the championship game for the first time in network history, with ABC also carrying the event. ESPN has already outlined extensive programming and storytelling designed to build anticipation well before the game itself.The timing also feeds into a broader conversation about the Super Bowl calendar. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday, particularly because fans already tend to treat Presidents' Day weekend as a natural extension of Super Bowl celebrations.Commissioner Roger Goodell has previously discussed how changes to the NFL schedule could eventually push the Super Bowl toward Presidents' Day weekend. In comments cited in the original report, he said:"I think if you went to 18 weeks regular season that would probably occur," Goodell said at the time. "It is possible somewhere in the calendar. Could happen before that just because of the calendar, the way it lays out.But I think 18 weeks would get you to that point, and I think it would be a really great move."For now, February 14, 2027 remains a one-of-a-kind collision between football and romance. The NFL has confirmed the date, and fans have plenty of time to decide whether Super Bowl Sunday will be a date-night disaster, a couples' tradition or simply the perfect excuse to order wings and watch football together.
Article Summary: Super Bowl LXI is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine's Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday.

Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC, while Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.But there is a big gap, and public net-worth numbers are best seen as estimates, not audited financial statements. Lesnar’s contracts in the modern era, UFC purses and limited-appearance model allowed him to make individual paydays that were much larger than what was generally available to wrestlers during Flair’s peak years. Meanwhile, Flair continues to earn from his name, appearances, licensing and wrestling-related projects, despite the financial difficulties that have beset his wealth over the years.Brock Lesnar seems to be in a better financial state at the moment. Celebrity Net Worth estimates his net worth at $10 million, whereas NDTV reported an estimate of $17 million in June 2026. Other outlets have published higher numbers, a testament to the uncertainties that come with calculating celebrity net worth.Ric Flair is worth much less. His net worth has been estimated to be $500,000 by Celebrity Net Worth, but other estimates online have put the figure at a much higher number.The variation reflects the absence of publicly verified personal financial records, and the challenge of calculating assets, liabilities, royalties and ongoing income for a longtime entertainer.Lesnar’s wealth is intrinsically tied to his ability to command top dollar. He was an instant star in WWE after debuting in 2002, but he later moved away from the wrestling world to try his hand at the NFL and mixed martial arts before returning to WWE as an established crossover star.Lesnar’s career in WWE has been as much about scarcity as it has been about star power. He was often employed on a limited schedule around major storylines and premium live events for most of his later career instead of working weekly.Lesnar’s UFC career distinguished his money story from most WWE stars. After leaving professional wrestling, he came into MMA and immediately became a big draw. Beating Randy Couture for the heavyweight championship at UFC 91 made him a legit heavyweight champion and gave him a serious bump in commercial appeal.Lesnar has also earned money from endorsements and appearances. Jimmy John’s and other commercial deals are among his previous endorsement deals, and his celebrity status has helped his value outside the ring.He has also kept his lifestyle very private. Recent reports have pointed out that he prefers a rural lifestyle and owning vast amounts of land, rather than the high-profile celebrity lifestyle that many sports stars enjoy.Ric Flair’s financial story started in an era when the economics of professional wrestling were very different. The Nature Boy became one of the defining stars of the National Wrestling Alliance, World Championship Wrestling and WWE, headlining big events and winning championships through a career that spanned several decades.Flair made a ton of money in his time with WCW. One published estimate puts his WCW earnings from 1996-2000 at about $1.95 million. But the size of his earnings did not translate directly into lasting wealth because of taxes, legal obligations, medical expenses and other financial pressures.He also made a lot of money from his WWE career. Flair was a wrestler, manager and personality and stayed a close associate of the company for years. In 2005, during a divorce hearing, it was revealed that his annual WWE salary was reportedly around $500,000, showing how much he could make from wrestling even later in his career.Of the two stars, Flair's financial history is the starkest contrast. Celebrity Net Worth states that in 2000, the IRS filed a lien of more than $870,000 against him, and his further tax problems damaged his finances. The same source reports that in 2019 there was a major medical emergency that resulted in a medical bill of approximately $1.8 million.These pressures help explain why lifetime earnings and current net worth can look so dramatically different. Making millions in a career doesn’t always translate to keeping millions after taxes, debts, medical expenses and other costs.Lesnar’s future financial prospects will probably continue to be linked to his standing as a top-tier combat sports attraction. As his active wrestling career is changing, his name still has value for special appearances, merchandise, licensing and media projects.Flair’s earning model is a unique one. At 77, his money-making opportunities are increasingly linked to his legacy rather than regular ring competition. He still turns up at wrestling events, signs autographs and does other promotional stuff.Lesnar has a path to victory in the modern economics of sports and one of the rare WWE-to-UFC crossover careers. Flair’s financial legacy isn’t so much the wealth he has today, but the incredible value he brought to pro wrestling in terms of sales. Their careers demonstrate two different paths a wrestling superstar can take to earn money: Lesnar with premium modern contracts and crossover sports earnings, and Flair with longevity, character, championships and lasting brand recognition.
Article Summary: Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC. Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.

Article Title: “I just want to share that with all these little kids”: How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need
Article Text:
How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need(Getty)

Sophie Cunningham turned her WNBA fines joke into a $10,182 act of kindness

Sophie Cunninghum past Ronald McDonald House connection goes back to 2015
